transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-04
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~55 mins
Attendees: Marissa Chen (Redwood AE), Devon Patel (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood), Rachel Turner (Oakridge - Head of Security), Samir Basu (Oakridge - Identity Engineer), Claire Nguyen (Oakridge - Platform), Tom Alvarez (Oakridge CTO)

Auto-summary (auto):
- Purpose: Review SSO (SAML) integration approach, SCIM provisioning flow, and least-privilege RBAC role matrix for Redwood integration into Oakridge infra.
- Primary concerns: BYOK/KMS integration, audit log retention/location, group->role mapping, deprovisioning latency, SOC2 evidence paths.

Transcript:
[00:00] Marissa (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — we have Devon and Luis from my side. Could you confirm oakridge attendees?
[00:10] Rachel (Oakridge): Rachel here. Samir, Claire, Tom in the call. Thanks.
[00:14] Marissa: Great. High level: we'll cover SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, how we map groups to Redwood roles, and then the audit/logging and encryption/BYOK discussion. Feel free to interrupt.
[00:28] Devon (Redwood SE): I'll jump into the technical flow; we'll show the assertion claims we expect and SCIM delta behavior.
[00:34] Samir (Oakridge): Perfect. Our identity stack is Okta for primary, sometimes Azure AD. We do SAML 2.0 with signed assertions, and SCIM 2.0 for provisioning. Our compliance team wants minimum privilege and proof of deprovisioning within 15 minutes.
[00:48] Devon: Okay, good context. Redwood supports SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SAML, signed assertions, and we have a role-attribute claim mapping option. For deprovisioning via SCIM, we listen to user delete and group membership changes and then shrink session tokens — note there's a short TTL on active tokens.
[01:10] Rachel: How short is that TTL? If a user is removed in Okta, we need them out of your console within 15 minutes.
[01:18] Luis (Redwood): Current default session token TTL is 30 minutes in hosted mode, but for enterprise/private customers we can support session revocation hooks and shorten to ~5-10 minutes. There's an option for immediate session invalidation if you run Redwood Private with an agent, but that requires a small integration.
[01:36] Samir: That immediate invalidation would be nice, what's the integration overhead?
[01:40] Luis: It's a webhook-based revocation or a push to your session store; the Private deployment has a control plane call that you can trigger from your IdP SCIM connector. It's a small infra change — we'll share the runbook.
[01:52] Claire: On RBAC, we want to avoid a flat 'admin' role. We need a role matrix: read-only, developer, ops, admin, billing. How does group->role mapping work?
[02:04] Devon: We recommend group attribute mapping using a roles claim or SCIM group sync. Example: Okta group 'redwood-dev' -> Redwood role 'developer'. We'll share a SCIM mapping spreadsheet. We also support attribute-based mapping if you include a roles attribute in the SAML assertion.
[02:20] Tom (Oakridge): Does SCIM support delta sync? We can't do full sync every minute.
[02:25] Devon: Yes SCIM delta is supported; we process PATCH/PUT operations and group membership deltas. For our hosted offering, we poll with a short window, but for Dedicated/Private we can take push-based events.
[02:38] Rachel: Audit logs — where do they live? Retention? Can we forward to our SIEM?
[02:45] Marissa: Redwood provides both in-console audit with retention tiers and a log export stream. For enterprise customers you can push events to your S3 bucket, or we can forward to Splunk/Datadog via HTTPS. Retention is configurable; default 90 days, options to extend to multi-year via add-on. SOC2 docs show controls around log integrity.
[03:06] Samir: Is log storage encrypted with customer-managed keys?
[03:09] Luis: Yes, for Private deployments we support BYOK using your KMS/HSM. For hosted we offer a customer-managed key option where keys are in your cloud KMS (AWS KMS or GCP KMS); on-prem HSMs can be integrated for Dedicated. There is a note that not every object is encrypted with BYOK by default — we'll provide a table in the security whitepaper.
[03:30] Claire: Data residency — we need logs and content stored in EU region only. How do you guarantee that?
[03:36] Devon: We support regional tenancy; for hosted we can pin your org to eu-west region, with metadata and token storage kept in-region. For full control you can run Redwood Private in your VPC. We'll include our region data flow diagram in the follow-up.
[03:50] Rachel: SOC2 — do you share the type 2 report and scope?
[03:54] Marissa: Yes, we'll share the SOC 2 Type II report and the summary of scope. It covers our hosted control plane and certain infra. For Private deployments we provide a responsibility matrix.
[04:05] Tom: A question on SAML attributes — we want the role claim to be authoritative and sent as a list. Does Redwood accept a multivalued attribute?
[04:12] Devon: Yes, we accept multivalued role attributes and will map them to multiple roles. If both SCIM and SAML provide role info we have a precedence order — SCIM wins for provisioning state, SAML for session-level claims. We'll document that precedence.
[04:30] Rachel: Deprovisioning proof — we need an auditable trail showing user X removed and their tokens revoked.
[04:36] Luis: Audit log entries include user lifecycle events, token revocation actions, and correlation IDs. We can produce a report export for compliance. For higher assurance customers we support signed audit bundles.
[04:50] Samir: Okta specifics — how do we configure attribute statements? We use the 'groups' attribute plus a custom 'roles' claim.
[04:58] Devon: In Okta, you'll configure the app to include role and groups claims; we will accept either. For SCIM, make sure group object has a member list and your group names follow agreed naming convention. We also handle SCIM patch operations like add/remove members.
[05:12] Samir: Any rate limits on SCIM operations? We might do bulk updates during org changes.
[05:17] Luis: We have rate limits to protect the control plane; for enterprise customers we can raise the limits or supply a batch import API. We'll include batch import guidance.
[05:28] Claire: Regarding encryption in transit and at rest — do you support TLS 1.3 only?
[05:33] Devon: We support TLS 1.2 and 1.3; we recommend 1.3. For inter-service communication inside private deployment it's mTLS by default.
[05:42] Rachel: KMS audit — we need proof key rotation and key use logs.
[05:46] Luis: When using customer-managed KMS, key control and rotation is in your KMS logs. We capture reference to key IDs and store encryption metadata in our audit logs; we don't store raw keys.
[05:58] Tom: What about least-privilege for API keys? We want per-route scoping and a way to restrict embeddings endpoints vs generation.
[06:05] Devon: Redwood supports per-token scopes; you can create API tokens scoped to models, routes, and time windows. For tighter controls, service tokens can be constrained to a set of routes and IP ranges.
[06:18] Rachel: How do you prove who invoked an API action? Is there token attribution in audit logs?
[06:23] Luis: Audit logs include token IDs, user associations, originating IP, and request traces. For SSO users we can map back to user principal.
[06:33] Samir: If we do SCIM deprovisioning, what is the typical delay to remove access from a long-lived streaming session?
[06:39] Devon: Streaming sessions may persist longer because of delta in KV caches; we revoke new token issuance immediately. For the actual active stream you can set a server-side idle timeout or forcefully terminate if you need immediate kill. There's a small window — we'll note it in the runbook.
[06:56] Claire: We'd like a role matrix template — we want to map existing Okta groups to Redwood roles and list allowed actions for each role.
[07:03] Marissa: We'll share a template with recommended least-privilege defaults and examples from other logistics customers.
[07:12] Rachel: On the topic of compliance, will Redwood provide encryption attestations and a SOC 2 scope for hosted storage?
[07:18] Marissa: Yes, deliverables will include SOC2 Type II, ISO summary, and encryption architecture doc. We'll also send a responsibility matrix distinguishing customer-managed vs Redwood-managed controls.
[07:30] Tom: Any blockers for us to start a PoC? We want to provision a dev tenant and run SCIM imports and a few SAML logins.
[07:36] Devon: No blockers. We'll need an Okta dev subdomain and a service account for SCIM. We'll provide an integration checklist.
[07:44] Rachel: One more — session replay or content logging. We do not want message payloads stored beyond necessary. How do you handle PII and chat content?
[07:53] Luis: By default we store inference logs for N days for billing and quality. For regulated customers we can turn off content persistence and only store metadata. We also support field-level redaction and deterministic hashing for certain PII fields.
[08:08] Samir: Is redaction done client-side or server-side?
[08:11] Luis: Both options exist. We can provide client-side SDK helpers to hash before sending, or server-side redaction pipelines if you need more flexibility.
[08:21] Marissa: Quick pivot to procurement concerns — Tom, you mentioned wanting a cust KMS and a specific SLAs?
[08:27] Tom: Yes, 99.9% uptime SLA for dedicated workloads, and we want a defined RTO for incident response. Also need contract language around encryption obligations.
[08:36] Marissa: Our enterprise agreements cover Dedicated capacity SLAs. We'll flag legal to provide draft language.
[08:42] Claire: Can we integrate with our centralized audit archive? We use an S3 with bucket policies and our SIEM ingests from there.
[08:49] Devon: Absolutely, we can drop log bundles into your S3, or forward events to your HTTPS endpoint. We'll send the schema for log events.
[08:58] Rachel: Are there any known gotchas with Azure AD vs Okta for role claim behavior?
[09:03] Devon: Azure AD sends group IDs by default whereas Okta sends group names; you may need to map ID->name for Azure. Also Azure sometimes limits group claims in SAML — you might need group filtering or to use SCIM as source of truth.
[09:18] Samir: Can we limit API keys to IP allowlists?
[09:21] Luis: Yes, per-token IP restrictions are supported.
[09:24] Marissa: Time check — about 40 minutes left for follow-ups and deep dive, anything else high level?
[09:31] Rachel: Let's jump into a short demo of how mapping works.
[09:35] Devon: (screen share) Here is the RBAC page in the console — you can create roles with fine grain permissions. I'm toggling a 'developer' role and showing allowed routes. You can also create dynamic roles based on group attributes.
[10:00] (Demo noise, some audio overlap)
[12:15] Devon: Back to SAML attributes — we accept custom namespace attributes too. Important: if you include groups in SAML, keep the payload small; large group lists are better via SCIM.
[12:38] Claire: For large orgs we plan to manage groups in Okta and only send role assertions for session-level enforcement. Provisioning via SCIM will still sync membership.
[13:02] Devon: That's a recommended pattern — SCIM for provisioning, SAML for session claims.
[13:12] Rachel: Can we get a sample log showing a user removal event and token revocation?
[13:17] Luis: We'll attach an anonymized sample in the follow-up.
[13:21] Tom: One more around keys — if we rotate keys in KMS, how do you handle re-encrypting stored blobs?
[13:27] Luis: For customer-managed KMS, rotation is normally a KMS operation where data keys are rewrapped. We'll provide the documented lifecycle; some objects are re-encrypted lazily on access. We'll include a table of rewrap semantics.
[13:44] Marissa: Okay I'm going to summarize action items and next steps.
[13:48] Marissa: Redwood will send SOC2, ISO notes, security whitepaper, SCIM mapping template, demo recording, and runbook for session revocation and BYOK. Oakridge will provision dev Okta tenant, invite the service account, and confirm the required retention and residency requirements.
[14:05] Rachel: Sounds good. Any blockers on our side? We'll aim to have the Okta dev tenant by 11/11.
[14:12] Marissa: Great — we'll schedule a technical PoC check-in for next week. Thanks everyone.
[14:16] (meeting ends)
